title: Rest at home
hook: Martha serves, Mary sits: a home that lets you rest, and the old debate over which sister was right
tomorrow: three strangers in the heat of the day. why did an old man run?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: repair. Jacob walked toward his brother's face, and Esau ran. Today, a home that lets you set the work down.
screen: `REPAIR.` → `A HOME THAT LETS YOU SET IT DOWN.`

segments.voice: A guest is coming, the kitchen is chaos, and one person is doing all of it. Luke's Gospel has that scene. Jesus comes to the house of two sisters. Martha is busy with all the serving. Her sister Mary sits at his feet and listens. Martha comes to him: doesn't it bother you that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me. The answer, in the King James words: "Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her."
screen: `ONE PERSON DOING ALL OF IT.` → `MARTHA SERVES, MARY SITS.` → `ONE THING IS NEEDFUL.`

segments.voice: So Mary wins? Readers have argued about it, and Martha's side deserves its best case. Someone has to cook. Welcoming a guest is holy work, and Martha is the one doing it. The medieval preacher Meister Eckhart took her side in a sermon on this very passage: he praised Martha as the one who had learned to stay close to God in the middle of work, while Mary, he suggested, was still learning. Other readers made Mary the picture of the contemplative life: the listening that comes first. Now notice what Jesus doesn't say. He doesn't call the serving bad. He says Martha is careful and troubled about many things, and that one thing is needful. The trouble is the many, not the work. That's a teaching Christians draw from the scene: make room to sit and listen, even in a busy house, because rest doesn't come from the list being finished. It comes from turning, for a while, to the one thing. A home can help with that: one chair, one corner, where nothing asks you to serve.
screen: `THE BEST CASE FOR MARTHA.` · `ECKHART TAKES MARTHA'S SIDE.` · `MARY: THE LISTENING THAT COMES FIRST.` · `THE TROUBLE IS THE MANY, NOT THE WORK.` · then, large: `A RESTFUL CORNER.`

segments.voice: Look around the room you're in and find one spot that could be a resting corner: a chair, a step, a patch of floor by a window. Move there if you can, or simply look at it. Then let the many things wait while you sit.
Rest at home: a place where the many things wait and the one thing gets your attention. Mary's place at his feet.
Keep this close: a restful corner, where Martha's real work gets set down for a while. Day 1718, done.
